title: I am genuinely confused as to how people defend Pasolini

commenti.body: We live in a world where that is gross and illegal. Well, in some countries. But from about the dawn of time until like forty years ago, it was quite normal for men to date teenage girls. Don’t get me wrong, I’m not saying we should go back to those days, but a little perspective goes a long. I say this not knowing the details about their relationship not would I think of defending or prosecuting a person based on what little I know.

>girls

Not quite Pasolini's tempo.
[removed]

Well originally some people liked it because they liked torture porn. Others liked it because it was communist and they like communism. And now some people like it because it’s in the cannon and they like things that are in the cannon. 

But yeah it’s unwatchable and the criticism it generates is either facile (fascism bad. capitalism bad. this movie shows fascist being bad) or gross Freudian nonsense so I’m far from convinced it’s a worthwhile intellectual exercise
Babe wake up new dialectics just dropped

Well it’s always about can you separate the art from the artist. 

For Salo, I think it’s definitely the lighter side of that question. In the end it’s the movie is about Nazi torturing teens and eating poop. Separating that from the director is definitely easier than other films. For example, film like Manhattan is definitely the harder side of the question, where is really just Woody Allen telling you, “hey, maybe dating a minor when you’re 41 is not as bad as it seems” that’s definitely the harder question.

Regarding ***Salò***, I haven't seen the film so I wouldn't be qualified to defend it on artistic terms, but I'd just like to offer this short film made by Mark Kermode which debates its value and argues that it's not exploitative or pornographic. 

[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Zf7UgXAh-nY](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Zf7UgXAh-nY)

I think there's room for the consideration that whatever Pasolini's failings in his personal life, he did not intend the film to be an extension of those desires of his for young men, but rather a more impersonal framing of fascism as a violent abuse. 

So on the whole I wouldn't be in favour of judging the film based on his criminal behaviour, as they don't seem related.
[removed]
Salo is literally the only Pasolini film not to mention it is literally the only film with ABSOLUTELY SHOCKING imagery!
The blonde one or the tan one? hummina hummina humina awoooga  ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°)

No. Because I can separate the art from the artist. Sometimes awful people make brilliant, beautiful things. Just like sometimes good people make terrible things. Do you argue that people should like shitty films because the filmmaker is a humanitarian or supports good causes or is a nice person?

The OP is about Salò. And Salò isn’t a film “with” shocking imagery, it solely consists of it.

And let’s not forget it’s not just a Pasolini (pedophile) film. It’s also a Sade (OG sadist, pervert) book of even purer and more unambiguous torture porn. Pasolini, as far as I can tell, unironically admired the book.

Your comments are unfair on a movie that was made with a serious intent, and is clearly not just 'torture porn'. Whatever its outcome, and I haven't been able to stomach watching it, it's clear that the artistic aim was to frame power structures like fascism as a Sadean extravaganza of abuse. So not just salivating over young victims getting tortured as in some VHS shocker. 

It's not just 'fascism bad' either. It's 'fascism uniquely monstrous with pathological desire and rage'. 

***The Zone of Interest*** also posits the concept that 'fascism is bad' but takes the opposite tack, that it is bad in a way that is humdrum and ordinary, an extension of normal people's indifference to suffering. 

Whichever is more correct as an analysis (my feeling is that it's the latter) they are both different ways of framing the examination, which is by no means superfluous in our time, of what is the nature of fascism? 

Fascism is not some far-off fairytale bogieman, it's in the next street over. So what it means and what motivates it is not a non-question.
You have any proof that Sade was a sadist?
[removed]

The guy died in 1975. I never met him and only know the basics about his life and politics. I have seen a dozen of the movies he has directed because he’s a canonical filmmaker and his work moves me. *The Decameron* is one of the greatest movies I have ever seen and *The Gospel According to Matthew, Accatone* and **Oedipus Rex* are up there as well. He also penned the screenplays for Fellini’s *La dolce vita* and *Nights of Cabiria.* I can’t imagine missing out on these films.
Or Luc Besson making a movie where a child comes onto an adult.

No and I agree with you to an extent. Polanski’s past actions aren’t going to stop me from streaming Rosemary’s Baby as one of my favorite horror movies but, for me, in modern contexts, I do think you have to accept the fact that as a consumer with buying power if you were hypothetically going to pay to see a new Roman Polanski film in theater, you are financially supporting a pedophile.

> fascism uniquely monstrous with pathological desire

Still very broad imo. 

Of course, you can go straight to Pasolini if you want a more specific reading of the allegory. 

Why so much shit eating? Because “industrial foods” are shit. Wow. That’s the kind of insight you can only find either by examination of the most transgressive and intellectual art, or by reading instagram reel comments. 

Personally think it’s lame that The Zone of Interest is actually about the horrors of the holocaust. I think it should be about the directors aesthetic dissatisfaction with Ragu spaghetti sauce.

Sure. And I'm fine with that. 


If you use a smart phone you are financially supporting slave labor. If you pay taxes in America you support global industrial warfare. If you drink coca cola at the movies you support a company that hires hit squads to murder labor activists.


If I wanted to be absolutely pure with my ethics and consumption I'd have to be living on a farm, on land that wasn't taken from previous people, and wouldn't be able to enjoy things that I enjoy because I'd have to measure everything against a purity test.


Sometimes I'm okay with giving like $.50 to someone I think is a bad person because their art is good. The world is a very imperfect place.

Sure and I’m not necessarily judging anyone for doing so. 

No one saying be absolutely pure with ethics (as that’s not possible), or that the world isn’t fundamentally corrupt, but I’m reading your perspective as “everything I do supports greed or someone evil so I shouldn’t worry about it at all” which i personally find pretty cynical.

It’s basically the political “what about ___” argument. I get that there are omnipresent brutal corporations that operate with no semblance of decency. And people can do what little they can as consumers to stay informed and try to pick the lesser of evils. But I just don’t think “you own a iPhone but won’t support Polanski?” Is a very compelling argument personally.
No I’m arguing that a film made by a real life pedophile that puts real life minors in exploitative sexual situations could easily be considered CP and therefore illegal

Then report the Criterion Collection to your government for distributing child pornography??


Somehow *Salo* has *not* been considered kiddie porn for decades. But if you have new evidence that it is, besides the icky feeling you get from it, that would be a major world cultural event.


Just cause you find something morally questionable or objectionable doesn't necessarily mean it's illegal. Or that other people shouldn't be allowed to see it and make a personal judgment themselves.

I'm saying it doesn't bother me. Some things do. This doesn't. I don't watch new Polanski movies because I don't think he still makes interesting movies. 


I'm saying that I find it somewhat funny and a hypocritical to an extent to have people argue that singular filmmakers who have done bad things should have their works ignored but will be fine with other things which are objectively as bad if not worse. It's not whataboutism as deflection, but looking at the context where people pick and choose their selective outrage and anger.


Obviously it all comes down to personal choices and personal lines in the sand. So I understand if people refuse to watch Polanski. But I also find it bemusing if they're also drinking a coke.

There was no Instagram or Twitter or Facebook in 1975. How many people were commenting on the perils of industrial junk food at that time? None. I know because my parents were stuffing that shit right into me back then. 

Though I don't think it's really appropriate to mix criticism of Western industrial food production into a dark political allegory-horror film about monstrous sexual abuse, it is still highly anachronistic to say 'Oh, you can see that take on Insta'. You simply couldn't. 

Try to put yourself into the time it was made, by all means criticise it on its own terms but don't distort it into something it isn't by forgetting its context.
